headword: {伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}

definitions.explanation: Handmade crafts and artisanal products that have been passed down through generations, using traditional techniques and materials. In Japan, certain crafts are officially designated and protected by law.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}は{伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}の{宝庫|ほうこ}だ。
examples.english: Kyoto is a treasure trove of traditional crafts.

examples.japanese: {伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{次|つぎ}の{世代|せだい}に{伝|つた}えたい。
examples.english: I want to pass on traditional craft techniques to the next generation.

examples.japanese: {後継者|こうけいしゃ}{不足|ぶそく}が{深刻|しんこく}で、{多|おお}くの{伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}が{消|き}えてしまう{危機|きき}にある。
examples.english: The shortage of successors is serious, and many traditional crafts are in danger of disappearing.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTES:
Japan officially designates certain crafts as {伝統的工芸品|でんとうてきこうげいひん} (traditional craft products) under the Traditional Craft Industries Promotion Act. Well-known examples include {輪島塗|わじまぬり} (Wajima lacquerware), {有田焼|ありたやき} (Arita porcelain), {西陣織|にしじんおり} (Nishijin weaving), and {江戸切子|えどきりこ} (Edo cut glass).

Many of these crafts face the challenge of {後継者|こうけいしゃ}{不足|ぶそく} (lack of successors), as younger generations often prefer other careers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}{品|ひん} (traditional craft product)
- {伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}{士|し} (traditional craft artisan)
- {伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}を{守|まも}る (to preserve traditional crafts)
- {伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}{体験|たいけん} (traditional craft experience/workshop)
